open_points.subject: agent-authority project selection
open_points.text: A10 says, “An operation on a project that names none uses the session's active project,” but never identifies which operations may omit `project_id`, especially operations such as withdrawal that name another record.
open_points.question: For each Cabinet Kernel operation, is `project_id` required, optional with active-project fallback, or derived from another record such as the pointer?
options: Allow omission for every project operation except those whose project is derived from another record
Enumerate only specific operations that may use the active project
Require `project_id` for all operations other than withdrawal
open_points.default_guess: Enumerate each operation explicitly; derive the project for withdrawal and allow active-project fallback for the other project-scoped operations.

open_points.subject: reuse of an ended agent-session identity
open_points.text: A11 says both that Kernel “never uses [an identity] again” so audit entries “mean one session” and that registering an ended identity “makes a new session with an empty set.” Registry removes the old record and keeps no tombstone.
open_points.question: Must Registry prevent reuse of an ended session identity, or may one identity denote multiple sessions and make old audit references ambiguous?
options: Keep a durable tombstone and refuse reuse
Permit reuse and define audit references as potentially naming several successive sessions
Trust Kernel not to reuse it while accepting that Registry cannot enforce the audit meaning
open_points.default_guess: Keep a durable non-secret tombstone and refuse registration of an ended identity.

open_points.subject: concurrent owner sessions
open_points.text: A13 says each successful sign-in “receives an owner session” but does not say whether another living owner session may coexist or whether a new sign-in ends earlier sessions.
open_points.question: How many owner sessions may be live, and what does a new sign-in or sign-out do to the others?
options: Allow any number; sign-out ends only the current session
Allow one; a new sign-in ends the previous session
Allow a bounded number with an explicit eviction rule
open_points.default_guess: Allow multiple sessions and make sign-out end only the session whose cookie was presented.

open_points.subject: owner-session cookie scope
open_points.text: A13 requires a cookie “only to Registry's own origin,” but browser cookies are not scoped by port and the text does not declare the cookie's Domain, Path, SameSite or complete Secure behavior.
open_points.question: What exact cookie scope and attributes implement “own origin,” including deployments where Registry is reached over local HTTP and remote HTTPS?
options: Use a dedicated hostname with a host-only `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/` cookie
Use a host-only path-scoped cookie and accept that sibling ports share the host cookie namespace
Forbid HTTP sign-in and require HTTPS everywhere
open_points.default_guess: Give the owner interface a dedicated hostname and use a host-only `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/` cookie.

open_points.subject: removed artifact types in read answers
open_points.text: A22 removes a type from the release's declared vocabulary while requiring existing pointers of that type to remain in list answers and the agent projection. State 1 describes artifact type as a closed vocabulary of the release.
open_points.question: How can current-release schemas represent a historical pointer whose type is no longer declared?
options: Keep a historical read vocabulary containing every formerly declared name and a smaller writable vocabulary
Represent pointer types as unrestricted stored text on reads but validate publishes against the current vocabulary
Never remove a name from the read vocabulary; mark it retired instead
open_points.default_guess: Separate the historical read vocabulary from the currently publishable vocabulary.

open_points.subject: uploaded files in other owner sessions after import
open_points.text: A16 and M11 say an uploaded file is dropped “when the import is accepted,” but several owner sessions may each hold a file and the text does not say whether acceptance in one session drops files held by the others.
open_points.question: When one session successfully imports and creates the migration closure, what happens immediately to uploaded import files and pending import confirmations in every other session?
options: Drop and invalidate all of them
Drop only the accepting session's file and leave the others until replacement or session end
Drop other files but leave their confirmations to fail when submitted
open_points.default_guess: Drop every uploaded import file and invalidate every pending import confirmation as part of closing the import operation.

open_points.subject: temporal validity of imported archived projects
open_points.text: A16 rejects a record changed, archived or superseded before its creation but does not cover a room added or pointer published after its project was archived, nor say whether an imported archived project's last-changed instant must be its archived instant.
open_points.question: Which cross-record time relationships must an imported project, its rooms and its pointers satisfy?
options: Refuse any room or pointer event after archival and require last-changed to equal archived time
Check only the pairwise inequalities explicitly listed and accept other source histories
Declare a complete import-specific chronology distinct from normal Registry transitions
open_points.default_guess: Refuse child events after archival and require an archived project's last-changed instant to equal its archived instant.

open_points.subject: import file digest
open_points.text: A16 binds the mapping, confirmation, closure and audit entry to “the file's digest” without declaring the digest algorithm or whether it covers the exact uploaded bytes or a parsed/canonical representation.
open_points.question: What digest algorithm and byte representation identify an import file?
options: SHA-256 of the exact uploaded bytes
A stronger specified digest of the exact uploaded bytes
A digest of a canonical parsed representation
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 over the exact uploaded bytes and compare the digest in constant time where it authorizes confirmation.

open_points.subject: secret length and equality
open_points.text: A17 requires every secret to be “at least 32 bytes long” and no two secrets to be equal, but does not define the configured representation, decoding or normalization used for those checks.
open_points.question: Are secrets raw bytes, encoded text decoded to bytes, or Unicode text, and on which representation are length, equality and authentication comparisons performed?
options: Require a fixed textual encoding such as base64url and compare decoded bytes
Treat the exact UTF-8 encoding of configured text as the secret bytes
Require raw binary secret files
open_points.default_guess: Require canonical base64url text, validate it strictly, and perform all checks on the decoded bytes.

open_points.subject: store and backup locations
open_points.text: A17 checks that both locations work but does not require the backup location to be distinct from, or non-overlapping with, the store location.
open_points.question: Which path relationships between the store, backup directory and temporary verification files are permitted?
options: Require distinct, non-overlapping resolved paths
Allow the backup directory beside but not inside the store path
Leave all layouts valid and require the backend to avoid recursion or overwrite
open_points.default_guess: Resolve paths and refuse equality, nesting or aliasing through symlinks.

open_points.subject: backup encryption format
open_points.text: A18 says each backup is encrypted with the backup key and integrity-checked after decryption, but declares no authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce rule, file format or corruption/authentication failure behavior.
open_points.question: What exact authenticated backup format and cryptographic construction must every backend use?
options: Specify an AEAD algorithm, random nonce, authenticated metadata and versioned envelope
Permit any release-fixed authenticated-encryption backend satisfying declared tests
Use encryption plus a separate keyed authentication code
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned AEAD envelope with a fresh random nonce and authenticated release and backup metadata.

open_points.subject: retention metadata after backup-key rotation
open_points.text: Older backups remain encrypted under old keys kept only in the owner's vault, while Registry must automatically determine which backups are more than 30 days old. The text does not say how Registry identifies a backup's key or reads its creation instant without that old key.
open_points.question: Where are the backup creation time and key identifier kept so automated retention and manual restore still work after key rotation?
options: Put authenticated non-secret metadata in a cleartext envelope header
Configure Registry with a keyring containing all still-needed keys
Use trusted filenames or filesystem timestamps and let the owner identify the key manually
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned cleartext header containing creation time and a non-secret key identifier, authenticated as AEAD associated data.

open_points.subject: audit sequence after restoration
open_points.text: M09 and A15 say sequence numbers are never reused and continue from the last number ever written, while A18 says restoration resumes from the backup's last number and post-backup entries are lost. Their sequence numbers can therefore be issued again.
open_points.question: After restoring an older backup, how is the global audit high-water mark recovered so a previously issued sequence number is never reused?
options: Persist the high-water mark outside backups and restore it separately
Allow a new audit epoch and make identity the pair of epoch and sequence
Permit reuse after disaster recovery and narrow the earlier invariant
open_points.default_guess: Introduce a durable audit epoch and identify/order entries by epoch plus sequence.

open_points.subject: migration closure after restoration
open_points.text: A18 permits restoring a backup made before the one successful import, but its reconciliation step mentions only Customer and project retention state. Such a restore loses M10 and makes A16's supposedly closed one-time import available again.
open_points.question: How is the fact of a previously successful migration restored or reconstructed when the selected backup predates it?
options: Keep the migration closure in separate disaster-recovery state
Provide an owner-only recovery action that reinstates the closure without importing
Permit another import after restoration and redefine “once” per restored history
open_points.default_guess: Keep independently recoverable evidence of the migration closure and reinstate it before Registry serves any interface capable of importing.

open_points.subject: old audit entries revived by restoration
open_points.text: A18's owner-only reconciliation lists Customers and projects but not an audit erasure performed after the backup. Restoring that backup revives entries A15 had erased by date.
open_points.question: Must disaster-recovery reconciliation reapply the governance cutoff to the restored audit log before normal service resumes?
options: Yes, require the owner to run the dated audit erasure during owner-only recovery
Automatically retain the latest audit cutoff outside the backup and apply it on restore
Accept revival until the next periodic review
open_points.default_guess: Require the current audit cutoff to be reapplied during owner-only recovery before service tokens are enabled.

open_points.subject: completion of restore reconciliation
open_points.text: A18 says the owner must bring records to their current retention state before enabling tokens, then says Registry “cannot list them or tell when this is done.” Nothing prevents tokens being configured before the required work is complete.
open_points.question: What enforces or records completion of the owner-only recovery reconciliation?
options: Add a durable recovery-pending gate cleared by an explicit owner confirmation
Rely solely on the owner's deployment procedure and describe the property as operational rather than a Registry invariant
Require a signed external recovery manifest that Registry applies
open_points.default_guess: Persist a recovery-pending state and refuse service-token startup until the owner explicitly completes and confirms reconciliation.

open_points.subject: query and command structural separation
open_points.text: A19 now says, “No value a caller gives ever becomes part of a query's or a command's structure; how the store's backend lowers this is the backend's.” No required test or backend contract establishes that lowering preserves the rule.
open_points.question: What backend obligation and verification demonstrate that caller values cannot alter query or command structure?
options: Require bound parameters for data values and allowlisted mappings for structural choices
Require a typed query API whose contract guarantees structural separation
Permit backend-specific escaping accompanied by backend-specific injection tests
open_points.default_guess: Require bound parameters for all data values and closed allowlisted mappings for any structural choice.

open_points.subject: scope of interpreted-input protection
open_points.text: A19 protects “a value a caller gives” from query or command structure, whereas A21 claims that no input becomes a query, command, template or “other interpreted structure.” It is silent about derived forms of caller input and interpreted structures other than queries and commands.
open_points.question: Does the prohibition cover transformed or derived caller data and every interpreter boundary, including templates, paths, regular expressions and configuration fragments?
options: Cover all data derived from caller input at every interpreter boundary
Cover only direct caller values used in database queries and operating-system commands
Enumerate the interpreter boundaries Registry actually has and state the rule for each
open_points.default_guess: Enumerate every interpreter boundary and apply the prohibition to both direct and derived caller-controlled data.

open_points.subject: security-review status after A19 changed
open_points.text: A21 says, “A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.” A19 is named by `injection_interpreted_input` and has changed, while the document still says “Security review: PERFORMED” and that the review is complete.
open_points.question: Has the injection review been repeated against the changed A19 rule, and what is the resulting accepted evidence?
options: Mark A21 reopened until a new review is recorded
Record a new performed review explicitly accepting the changed rule
Declare the wording change non-semantic and explain why its guarantees and tests are unchanged
open_points.default_guess: Mark A21 reopened and repeat the injection-interpreted-input review.

open_points.subject: security-review reopening after affected model changes
open_points.text: A21's reopening rule mentions only “a change to a decision a category names,” although the review's affected subjects include M11 and the import file, both changed here to carry mutable confirmation state and an uploaded personal-data file.
open_points.question: Do changes to an affected model or data classification also reopen the relevant browser, files, authorization and concurrency reviews?
options: Yes, any change to a listed decision or affected subject reopens its categories
Only decision text changes reopen the review
Define a materiality test and record why each model change does or does not reopen it
open_points.default_guess: Reopen every category that lists the changed model or data as affected.

open_points.subject: request-id retention after erasure
open_points.text: A01 says a request id is removed by anonymisation or erasure and a later create with it “is a new create.” R0-36 says a retried create never silently makes a second project or Customer.
open_points.question: After a Project is anonymised or deleted, or a Customer is erased, must its former request id remain reserved so an old retry cannot create a duplicate?
options: Keep a non-personal request-id tombstone and refuse or replay the old request
Allow reuse after erasure and narrow the no-duplicate guarantee
Reserve the id for a fixed, declared retention period
open_points.default_guess: Keep a permanent model-scoped request-id tombstone containing no erased values and refuse the retry.

open_points.subject: request-id collision across project authorization boundaries
open_points.text: A01 looks up a caller-supplied request id globally within a model and says a differing collision is refused and “the caller reads the record.” For a room or pointer, the colliding existing record may belong to a project outside Kernel's session set, while A10 checks only the project named by the new call.
open_points.question: What answer is returned when Kernel supplies a request id already attached to a room or pointer in a project outside its granted set?
options: Return the same not-found answer as an out-of-set project and reveal no record
Refuse with a generic request-id conflict without returning the existing record
Scope request-id uniqueness and lookup by authorized project
open_points.default_guess: Reveal no record and return the same not-found answer used for an out-of-set project.

open_points.subject: precedence inside an A04 check stage
open_points.text: A04 declares six ordered stages and says “the first failure is its answer,” but gives no order among multiple checks in the same stage, such as a blank pointer reference and unknown type in stage 4, or an archived project and ineligible customer in stage 6.
open_points.question: What exact refusal wins when two or more checks in the same stage fail?
options: Declare an operation-specific total order for every check
Return one generic error for all failures within a stage
Validate all checks in the stage and return a structured set of failures where disclosure rules permit
open_points.default_guess: Declare a fixed operation-specific total order, preserving A10's not-found concealment before all later checks.

open_points.subject: classification of pending import-confirmation inputs
open_points.text: The changed disclosure table classifies “the owner session, but for its uploaded import file” as `business_confidential`, while changed M11 stores a pending confirmation's bound inputs and A16 binds import confirmations to display names, Customer names and possible tax ids, which are `personal_data`.
open_points.question: What class applies to personal values retained as part of a pending import confirmation?
options: Classify each bound input by its underlying fact, making that part of the owner session `personal_data`
Store only a digest of the complete mapping so the pending confirmation contains no personal values
Classify the whole owner session as `personal_data` whenever such a confirmation is pending
open_points.default_guess: Store an authenticated digest of the complete mapping and keep the personal values only in the uploaded-file/mapping state already classified `personal_data`.
